Structure: lines 14-16 fix a finite, purely relational signature tau whose relation symbols all have positive arity, with no constant or function symbols. Lines 16-18 give a labeled n-element tau-structure the universe [n]={0,...,n-1}. Probability model: lines 18-19 define 'uniformly random' as the uniform distribution over all such labeled structures. The theorem at lines 25-27 draws A_n from that distribution. The switch to G(n,1/2) at lines 42-45 is announced as applying to that paragraph only, so the two models are not conflated.

thm:p03-fol-zero-one (lines 25-33) has status cited=Fagin1976 (status mechanism: handbook.sty line 25). It states that for every first-order tau-sentence, lim Pr[A_n |= phi] exists and lies in {0,1} when A_n is uniform over the labeled tau-structures on [n]. Lines 19-20 declare the vocabulary restrictions (finite, relational, positive arity, no constants or functions) to be part of the law. Lines 35-36 attribute the theorem to Glebskii-Kogan-Liogon'kii-Talanov 1969 and Fagin 1976. Lines 38-40 place built-in order or successor enrichments, and constants and function symbols, outside this formulation. The table row at line 184 repeats the exact scope. The status is cited, not presented as proved, which is the treatment-S standing. All bib keys resolve in handbook/bib/handbook.bib.

The ESO sentence form is defined at lines 67-78. The finite encoding convention is at lines 80-103: e(A)=a#b_1#...#b_r over {0,1,#}, with a the binary form of n and b_i the lexicographic characteristic words of length n^{m_i}. It also defines E(A), the shift from [n] to {1..n} and isomorphism invariance, and excludes the empty-vocabulary case (Fagin's NP_1) from the theorem. Theorem thm:p03-fagin (lines 105-112, cited=Fagin1974): for tau with at least one relation symbol and an isomorphism-closed class A, E(A) is in NP iff A is the class of finite models of an ESO tau-sentence. The order conventions are at lines 114-133: no built-in order; the NP-to-ESO direction guesses a linear order with least and greatest elements and successor; the machine direction guesses the tables; ordered LFP capture is the contrast. The P9 link is at lines 135-140. It points to sec:p09-finite-structures, titled 'Finite structures and descriptive complexity', which places thm:p03-fagin among the capture results at lines 171-183, and to thm:p09-fagin74-theorem6. All labels resolve and lie on the live route. The theorem is not presented as proved, and no domain is narrowed without being announced.
